component.name: org.nuxeo.agentic.ui.operations
component.documentation:
The Automation operations and chains that a business app's buttons may run on this server: the deployment's allow-list (plan decision 3, on its recommendation).
An app's actions.json names an operation for each button that runs one. The app registry, at /nuxeo/agentic-ui-apps/, serves the file with only the actions whose operation is on this allow-list, each with only the parameters it gives the operation, and says in its diagnostics what it left out. The operation AgenticUi.RunAction runs such an action on one record, and checks the allow-list again first, with the user's permission on the record.
The allow-list is the deployment's, not an app's: a file the server's administrators put in nxserver/config/, for one. A configuration package built by the package pipeline is refused if it contributes here. With no contribution, nothing is allowed.
Not the only control, and not a control over Nuxeo's own Automation endpoint, which still runs any operation a user may run, through /nuxeo/api/v1/automation/. A deployment that wants an allow-listed chain run only through a button closes that endpoint to it with a REST binding (org.nuxeo.ecm.automation.server.AutomationServer, point bindings).

extension-point.name: allowList
extension-point.documentation:
One operation or chain per element, by its id.
claims-adjusters
permission is the one the user needs on the record, besides Read: Write when left out. Each group, when there is one, is a group the user must be in one of. Each param is a parameter an app's action may give the operation: its name, and its type, string, boolean, long or double; a string is at most maxLength characters, 1000 when left out, and at most 10000. An action that gives a parameter not listed here is not served, and does not run. An entry that fails a check is not registered, and the log says why. A later contribution with the same id replaces it whole, and enabled="false" removes it.
